title: Sahiba Bali's Gurpurab post with Arjun Kapoor sparks dating buzz, fans wonder 'is it a soft launch?'
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Sahiba Bali posted a happy picture with Arjun Kapoor. Sahiba Bali and Arjun Kapoor's Gurpurab celebrations On the occasion of Gurpurab, Sahiba posted on Instagram and shared a story featuring Arjun Kapoor. The picture showed the two posing together with their heads covered. Soon, the photo made rounds on the internet, reigniting dating rumours as the two had first made headlines after being spotted together at the India vs England ODI at Lord's Cricket Ground in London.
Adding to this, Sharing the picture, Sahiba wrote, "I ate his half of the prashad too. Happy Gurpurab (sic)."
Meanwhile, After the photo was uploaded, followers were quick to take notice of Sahiba's cheeky caption and her playful reference to sharing Arjun's prashad.

Notably, The post was subsequently shared on Reddit, where users discussed whether the two were hinting at their relationship. While one user wrote, "Ik there are too many 'are they dating' posts for Sahiba, but this one is crazy and looks like a soft launch. More than a soft launch actually (sic)." Another commented, "It definitely looks like a soft launch (sic)." A third user added, "Ate half of his Prasad, yeah, definitely dating (sic)."

As per the latest buzz, Dating rumours involving Sahiba and Arjun began in late June 2026, when Sahiba shared a photo of Arjun on his birthday, calling him 'Sabka bestiee.' The photo immediately caught followers' attention. Their banter sparked speculation, and what added fuel to the fire was that, in July, the two were spotted sitting together in the stands, wearing matching shades of blue, during the India vs England third ODI in London.

In further updates, However, neither of them verified or denied the rumours. Later, Sahiba addressed the speculation through a series of sarcastic Instagram stories, putting a full stop to the dating rumours.
On top of that, Meanwhile, Arjun did not publicly respond to the rumours, either then or now.

Arjun Kapoor was most of late seen in the 2025 movie Mere Husband Ki Biwi, alongside Bhumi Pednekar and Rakul Preet Singh. On the other hand, Sahiba is known for films like Amar Singh Chamkila (2024) and Laila Majnu (2018).

title: Rakesh Roshan’s Filmkraft Productions leases Mumbai office space for Rs 7 lakhs monthly rent
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The commercial property is located on the 14 th floor of the C Wing of Lotus Corporate Park, along the Western Express Highway. The premises also come with three basement parking spaces. The leave-and-licence agreement was registered on November 13, 2026, with Filmkraft Productions represented by its director Rakesh Roshan, while Fuji Silvertech Concrete was represented by its Chief Strategy Officer, Brijmohan Gopaldas Soni.

Adding to this, As per the agreement, the licence period began on November 16, 2026, while the rental payments will commence from January 16, 2027. The tenant has been granted a two-month rent-free period to complete interior work and other fit-outs before occupying the premises.

Meanwhile, The agreement also includes an annual rent escalation of 5 per cent. Additionally, Fuji Silvertech Concrete has paid an interest-free, refundable security deposit of Rs 42 lakhs, equivalent to six months of the initial monthly rent.

Notably, With the annual increase, the monthly rent is expected to rise to Rs 7.35 lakhs in the second year, Rs 7.72 lakhs in the third year, Rs 8.10 lakhs in the fourth year and Rs 8.51 lakhs in the fifth year. The total rental income from the five-year agreement is estimated to be approximately Rs 4.5 crores, excluding applicable taxes and other charges.

As per the latest buzz, This latest transaction adds to the Roshan family’s recent property activities in Mumbai. In September 2026, Rakesh Roshan leased two commercial units in Andheri West, measuring a combined 5,574 square feet, to BeingU Studios Private Limited for an initial monthly rent of Rs 7.30 lakhs.
In further updates, Earlier, Rakesh Roshan and his wife Pramila Roshan had also leased their residential apartment in Mumbai’s JVPD Scheme for an initial monthly rent of Rs 5 lakhs.

On top of that, The filmmaker and his family have also been involved in several property acquisitions and sales across Mumbai and Pune. In November 2025, Rakesh and Pramila Roshan purchased five commercial units in Andheri East for a combined Rs 19.68 crores. These transactions reflect the family’s continued activity in the commercial and residential real estate market.
Meanwhile, Rakesh Roshan and Fuji Silvertech Concrete Private Limited could not be reached for comment regarding the latest lease agreement

title: Yeh Prem Mol Liya box office prediction: Sooraj Barjatya's Ayushmann-Sharvari film punches above its weight, set for ₹7-8 crore start
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Yeh Prem Mol Liya stars Ayushmann and Sharvari. Yeh Prem Mol Liya advance bookings Advance bookings for Yeh Prem Mol Liya began just three days before its rollout. Being a family-friendly movie with no superstar in the cast, it is not expected to fare too well in pre-sales. In fact, for such films, most of the opening-day earnings come from spot bookings, and word of mouth is crucial to sustain any momentum generated in the first weekend. According to Sacnilk, by noon on Wednesday, two days ahead of rollout, Yeh Prem Mol Liya has sold just over 10K tickets across India for its opening day, bringing in just under ₹ 30 lakh gross. The numbers surpass ₹ 50 lakh when pre-sales for the full weekend are factored in. The figures are bound to grow in the next two days, but may not surpass the ₹ 1-crore rupees mark.

Adding to this, However, low advance bookings are never worrying for a movie in this genre. Traditionally, unless featuring a superstar (like in Prem Ratan Dhan Paayo), Barjatya’s films have grown via word of mouth rather than taking a big upfront start. But Yeh Prem Mol Liya is still tracking well. According to trade insiders, its music and trailers have generated sufficient buzz to give the movie a ₹ 7-8 crore rupees net opening day start. Even if things go wrong, the movie should not open to less than ₹ 5 crore rupees. Good word of mouth can push it past even ₹ 9 crore rupees, some trade pundits say. This could lead to an opening weekend exceeding ₹ 25-30 crore rupees. For a movie as per reports made on a modest ₹ 60 crore rupees budget, this would be a great start.

Meanwhile, In Yeh Prem Mol Liya, Ayushmann plays Prem, a man who stands up for his new bride after she refuses to move in with her in-laws to take care of her own family. Sharvari plays the movie's female lead. The cast of Yeh Prem Mol Liya also includes Anupam Kher, Supriya Pathak Kapur, Seema Pahwa, Swanand Kirkire, Saumya Tandon, Shruti Seth, Shaad Randhawa, Girish Kulkarni and Rajesh Kumar.

Notably, Produced by Rajshri Productions in association with Mahaveer Jain Films, the movie marks Sooraj Barjatya's return to direction after Uunchai, which won a National Award. He has reunited with composer Himesh Reshammiya for the soundtrack after Prem Ratan Dhan Payo. Yeh Prem Mol Liya will rollout in theatres worldwide on November 27.

As per the latest buzz, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). With a good understanding of cinema and its trends, and a keen eye for detail, he continues to spark conversations around showbiz for readers around the world.

Ramayana: Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama in the movie. title: Ali Zafar says Tere Bin Laden struggled to find distributors for 2 years after 26/11 terror attacks, he was advised to return to Pakistan
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ali Zafar spoke about how his Bollywood debut Tere Bin Laden struggled after 26/11 attacks. more 'Everyone told me to come back' Speaking on Waseem Abbas' podcast, Ali recalled that choosing Tere Bin Laden for his debut was a daring decision in itself, given its subject and title. The situation became even more difficult after the 26/11 attack towards the end of the shoot.

Adding to this, He shared, "Woh jab shoot hui, it was quite a daring subject to do. Being a Pakistani, working in India and the first movie called Tere Bin Laden (laughs), jab mein shoot kar raha tha, incident ho gaya 26/11 ka (When we were shooting it, an incident took place. The 26/11 attacks happened), aur humare shoot ke 2-3 din reh gaye the (and we had just 2-3 days of shooting left). Sabne kaha wapas aa jao (everyone told me to come back), but meri bhi conviction thi ki mujhe yeh project khatam karna hai (but I was also convinced that I had to complete this project)."

Meanwhile, Ali eventually completed the remaining portions of the movie. However, the movie's journey to the big screen was far from over. According to the star, the makers spent nearly two years looking for distributors while also working on the edit and other aspects of post-production.

Notably, He shared, "Phir humaare baaki ka shoot Hyderabad Movie City mein khatam kar ke vaapas lauta (Then we completed the remaining shoot at Hyderabad Movie City and returned). Do saal woh movie distributors dhoond rahe the, edit kar rahe the wagera (For two years, they were looking for distributors and working on the edit and other post-production processes). Finally, jab woh 2010 mein rollout hui (when it was finally rolled out in 2010), there was critical acclaim."

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Abhishek Sharma, Tere Bin Laden is a 2010 satirical comedy starring Ali Zafar, Pradhuman Singh and Sugandha Garg. The movie follows Ali Hassan, a young Pakistani journalist who dreams of moving to the US. When he comes across a man who resembles Osama bin Laden, he comes up with a plan to shoot a fake video of the terrorist and sell it to a television channel to fund his American dream.

In further updates, Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. With a decade of experience across digital and print media, she covers Bollywood, Hollywood and web shows. A self-confessed cinephile who breathes Hindi cinema, Vibha can often be found sacrificing sleep after binge-watching films and web series. Though she holds a Commerce degree, she discovered her true calling in journalism after enrolling at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC). She began her career covering Delhi's cultural scene, food, nightlife, concerts, and city life at The Times of India, before moving into full-time entertainment journalism with India Today. At India Today, Vibha interviewed some of the biggest names in Bollywood and television while carving a niche for herself through movie reviews, opinion pieces, nostalgic features, star interviews, and trend-driven stories. She later brought her storytelling and editorial expertise to The Indian Express, where she continued to deepen her understanding of cinema through long-form entertainment explainers, retrospectives and feature writing. Now, as Assistant Editor at Hindustan Times Entertainment, Vibha continues to chronicle the world of movies and pop culture. Her work spans breaking entertainment news, exclusive interviews, star features, and stories that capture the conversations shaping Indian cinema.

title: Dr Shriram Nene says him and wife Madhuri Dixit don't boast about their success because they ‘grew up the hard way’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Dr Shriram Nene spoke about how him and wife Madhuri Dixit stay grounded. more 'Madhuri and I grew up the hard way' In a conversation with Khaleej Times, Dr Nene spoke about how Madhuri has remained grounded despite being one of the most successful actors in the country. He also credited her with bringing discipline to their household.

Adding to this, He shared, “My wife is a beacon of discipline and strength. Both of us are accomplished, but we don't wear our stripes on our sleeves, because we grew up the hard way. And when you do that, what you find is that you value people and things that you do, which are meaningful. And the conversations which are meaningful.”

title: Anupam Kher says Sooraj Barjatya's Yeh Prem Mol Liya is 'more progressive than any Western film', every Indian and foreigner should watch it
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Anupam Kher reviews Ayushmann Khurrana and Sharvari's Yeh Prem Mol Liya. more Anupam Kher reviews Yeh Prem Mol Liya On Tuesday, Anupam posted on Instagram to share a video message after watching the movie. Calling it “outstanding”, he lauded Sooraj's storytelling and shared, “It's such a progressive movie. It's a movie that every Indian and foreigner should watch. It's more progressive than any of the West films or European films. It educates you and entertains you, and it makes your eyes moist and makes you laugh. It's a magical movie.”
Adding to this, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Anupam Kher (@anupampkher)

Meanwhile, He went on to praise the filmmaker and Himesh Reshammiya's music in the movie, calling it one of the finest films he had seen. Anupam added, “I am very moved and touched after watching this movie.”

Notably, Sharing the video, the star also penned a heartfelt note for Sooraj. He wrote, “Sooraj, what a movie you have made! Sooraj Barjatya is among those people who still firmly believe that goodness always works. And over all these years, that belief of his has not changed one bit. Perhaps that is because Suraj practises that goodness in his own life.”

As per the latest buzz, Anupam also opened up that his mother had watched the movie and given it a perfect score of 100 out of 100. Recalling how Sooraj felt shy about receiving praise, the star shared he insisted that the filmmaker stand beside him for the video. He concluded his note by praising the movie's message about women's freedom to make their own life choices. He wrote, “What a wonderful movie! It conveys such an important message for today's times. I haven't seen a more beautiful example in a movie in a long time of what it means for women to have the freedom to make their own life choices. And Suraj puts this message across so effortlessly that you find yourself laughing, your eyes well up, and the message finds a place in your heart.”

In further updates, The romantic family drama marks Sooraj Barjatya's return to direction after Uunchai, which won a National Movie Award. The movie stars Ayushmann Khurrana and Sharvari in the lead roles, with Anupam Kher, Supriya Pathak, Seema Pahwa, Saumya Tandon, Shaad Randhawa and Swanand Kirkire in supporting roles.

On top of that, The movie revolves around Prem and Poorva, whose deep friendship gradually blossoms into romance. Instead of following the conventional tradition of the bride moving into the groom's home after marriage, the story explores what happens when the groom becomes part of the bride's family. title: Vijayan hails students' protest at Sanskrit University
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Vijayan hails students' protest at Sanskrit University The students were protesting against the suspension of 16 of their college mates for over two months and called off the agitation after the Kerala High Court allowed the suspended students to write their semester exams.

Adding to this, Vijayan, in a Facebook post on the occasion of the 32nd anniversary of the Koothuparamba firing incident in which five DYFI activists were killed and several others injured, accused the current UDF government of "handing over" education to the private sector and the Sangh Parivar.
Meanwhile, Paying tributes to those who died in the Koothuparamba firing, the former chief minister shared that it was an example of youth resistance against the commercialisation of education.

Notably, Five Democratic Youth Federation of India activists K K Rajeevan, Madhu, Shibulal, Babu, and Roshan were killed, and several others were injured in the police firing on protestors agitating against the then UDF government's education policy.
As per the latest buzz, Comrade Pushpan, who was seriously injured in the incident, was paralysed for three decades before his death in September 2024.

In further updates, "Koothuparamba Martyrs' Day reminds us of the history of the resistance raised by the Left against the moves to commercialise the education sector. Today, as the new UDF government is making intensive efforts to hand over the education sector to the private sector and the Sangh Parivar, the memories of the Koothuparamba struggle are becoming increasingly relevant," Vijayan shared.

On top of that, He further shared that the current student struggles, like the one at the Sanskrit University in Kalady, are a continuation of the resistance to protect educational rights and colleges.
"This is not just a need of the students, but a struggle to save the public education and future of the state," Vijayan, who is the opposition leader, shared.

During their conversation, Mukesh shared Ravie's audition video for the role of Lakshman in Ramayana. In the video, the star could be seen sporting a heavy beard and delivering dialogues from the Vanvas sequence. When Mukesh asked him how he had prepared for the audition, Ravie explained that Lakshman has a distinct essence. Having known the character since childhood, he shared he was familiar with his core attributes.
Adding to this, View this post on Instagram A post shared by IMDb India (@imdb_in)

Meanwhile, He added, "His core attributes are his service, his loyalty and his ethic. He has no need or aspiration to be in the forefront. So you have to keep telling, 'I'm here to serve'. Even during the audition the one thought that I kept telling myself was that 'I am here to serve.' When I auditioned and came back home, I stood in front of the temple and shared, 'This is the biggest movie I have ever auditioned for and I think the audition went well. Lord, I have made it so far, I don't need anything. Till today I had never come this far. That was enough source of gratiude for me."

Notably, Ravie added that he received no response for 15–20 days and was left waiting. The star opened up that he had almost accepted the outcome and decided to move on. However, Mukesh eventually texted him and asked him to meet Ramayana director Nitesh Tiwari. After another 15–20 days of silence, he met producer Namit Malhotra. Recalling what happened next, Ravie shared, "After that there was another 15-20 days of radio silence, and I had a fleeting thought in mind that maybe they might have found somebody better; no problem, let's move on with our lives. But after 15-20 days, I got another call and had a script reading where I got to know that Ranbir Kapoor is coming."

As per the latest buzz, He opened up that there was another 10-day wait after the script reading. It was only when they began shooting their first scene that he finally realised he was playing Lakshman in the movie.

In further updates, Ravie found an unexpected fan following overseas after playing Lakshman in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part 1. His performance has particularly caught the attention of audiences in Thailand, where followers have been sharing video edits of him on social media. Several Thai followers have been calling him ‘P'Ravie’ and even dubbing him an international heartthrob.

On top of that, One of his lines from the movie, ‘Tut gaya toh tut gaya’, delivered during the confrontation between Lakshman and Lord Parshuram after the breaking of Lord Shiva's bow at Sita's swayamvar, has become a social media favourite and inspired several memes.

Helmed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is a two-part mythological epic mounted on a reported budget of ₹ 4,000 crore rupees. Ramayana: Part 1 was rolled out on November 5 and received a positive critical response. Starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash and Ravie Dubey, the movie has been enjoying a strong run at the ticket-window. In just 20 days, it has crossed ₹ 970 crore rupees net in India and collected over ₹ 1,700 crore rupees worldwide. The second part is scheduled to rollout in theatres in 2028.

title: Ayan Mukerji confirms Brahmastra 2 is not shelved, wants to make it ‘more Indian’ after part 1's rocky landing
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ayan Mukerji with Ranbir Kapoor on the sets of Brahmastra. more Ayan Mukerji admits Brahmastra had a rocky landing Ayan was in Goa attending a session at the International Movie Festival of India ( IFFI ) with fellow filmmaker Basil Joseph. There, he spoke about Brahmastra's box-office fate and the ‘rocky’ landing it had. Starring Ranbir Kapoor and Alia Bhatt, Brahmastra collected over ₹ 435 crore rupees worldwide, but it was only a moderate success due to its reported ₹ 350-crore rupees budget. The audience and critics' reactions to the movie were also mixed.

Adding to this, Talking about the movie's reception, Ayan shared at IFFI, “With Brahmastra , it was a slightly rockier landing. There were things that people liked about the movie a lot, but there were certain things that they didn't like. I don't think the audience fails the movie. What they sense in a movie, you always have to respect it, even if that doesn't go in your favour. Our audiences are very smart. If there are things they didn't like, we definitely need to improve our storytelling.”

Meanwhile, Ayan shared he was influenced by Hollywood spectacle movies while making the first part but gradually moved towards Indian spirituality, which is why the title of the movie was eventually changed from Dragon to Brahmastra.

Notably, “I hope that we can make Brahmastra 2 even more Indian. What happened with me when I specifically began with Brahmastra, I think for me there were certain Western influences in my mind when it began. Because there were stories from the West which I enjoyed, Harry Potter, The Lord of the Rings to give you an example,” he added.

As per the latest buzz, Rolled out in 2022, Brahmastra Part 1: Shiva starred Ranbir, Alia, and Mouni Roy, along with Amitabh Bachchan in an extended cameo. Superstars Shah Rukh Khan and Nagarjuna also appeared in cameos. The movie was the first instalment of a planned trilogy with Ranbir playing Shiva, an orphaned Mumbai DJ with pyrokinetic (fire) powers. It established the Astraverse, a planned cinematic universe for Brahmastra.
In further updates, The second part, titled Brahmastra Part 2: Dev, was originally meant to rollout in 2026, but no work has begun on it yet. There is no update on when the movie will go on floors.

On top of that, Asked why they didn't shoot all three parts simultaneously, Ayan Mukerji admitted that they did not have the budget to do so. “Each team of producers and director has different circumstances and budgets. For us on Brahmastra, we couldn't have afforded to make Brahmastra 2 along with part 1. We had it in our minds, but we definitely needed part 1 to take that step,” he shared.

title: Families protest as police seal wedding venues in Sainik Farms after Delhi HC order
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Families allege the sealing drive led to last-minute cancellations and indefinite wedding postponements. (Representative file photo) more Families allege the sealing drive led to last-minute cancellations and indefinite wedding postponements.

Adding to this, On November 19, the high court gave the directions after a petition by a local organisation complaining of illegal marriage venues and banquet halls, those without any fire safety clearance or statutory permissions from the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD). The judge noted that for the safety of the people attending the functions at the venues, there should be an immediate suspension of events and commercial activities at the venues. The court also noted that these places can resume hosting events once they get necessary approvals.

Meanwhile, On Monday and Tuesday, as the Delhi Police started sealing the banquet halls without any prior notice, many families who had pre-booked these venues were left in disarray as they had no venue to host their function, lost all their money in deposits and other wedding expenses.
Notably, Senior police officials shared they sealed seven venues by Tuesday afternoon.

As per the latest buzz, Ravita Saha was supposed to get married on Tuesday but instead she was protesting outside the venue. Her father, Ram Lakhan Saha, shared, “We had put in all our money and all of the arrangements were done. She was supposed to get married today. Now, what do I tell all my family members, in laws and the groom? My daughter is broken. Her wedding procession was ready but we had nowhere to go.”

In further updates, Another woman, Aarti Singh, shared, “My wedding is supposed to happen in ten days. We had to pay for everything three months back only. Now, on Tuesday, we found the venue being locked and sealed. We had no idea. My parents are trying but we are not able to find any other venue. The venue people also didn’t inform us. They are not even giving a refund. Also, its peak wedding season in Delhi. Where will I get married now?”
On top of that, The families marched from the W lane in Sainik Farms where most of the venues had been sealed.

“My daughter’s wedding is on Tuesday night. My daughter was in the salon. My husband and I were checking the decoration and caterers when we found the venue is being sealed and soon will be demolished. I paid for the wedding with all my savings six months back. My daughter is heartbroken and hasn’t stopped crying. We need justice. We have been humiliated in front of our family members. The wedding was supposed to happen in three hours. Can’t the government or Delhi Police give us some time?”

title: Pratik Gandhi says he doesn't want to portray Gandhi as a Mahatma, explains his approach to biopics | Interview
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Pratik Gandhi spoke about his process while choosing roles. more In an exclusive interaction with Hindustan Times, Pratik refrained from revealing much about his soon-to-release projects but opened up about his experience shooting Madgaon Express, recalling how the camaraderie and madness on sets were just as evident as they were on screen. The star also spoke about the responsibility of portraying historical figures, his creative process while choosing roles and why he continues to enjoy collaborating with Hansal Mehta. Read on:

Adding to this, We had so much fun. In fact, everything you saw on screen was actually happening on set. The camaraderie and friendship between the three of us – me, Divyendu and Avinash – we genuinely had a lot of fun.

Meanwhile, Kunal Kemmu was extremely clear about what he wanted. I guess he spent a lot of time working on the script itself. By the time he decided to direct it, he knew exactly how much to shoot, which angles to use and where to cut each scene. The end point was also extremely clear in his mind. Kunal also has a great knack for humour. His style of humour is evident in every line and sequence. His sense of humour connects with youngsters.

Notably, The best part about the movie was that all the actors were extremely comfortable, confident and secure in their respective characters, which is very important in comedy. On the sets, I made two very good friends. And we explored all of Goa after the shoot.

As per the latest buzz, I think my process is extremely organic. If I read a script or hear a narration and connect with the story and the character, I try to understand whether there is scope for me to add value to it and whether it will add value to me as an star. That's the only thing that helps me decide whether to take up a project or not. I don't look at other things that are beyond my control.

In further updates, As an star, I have always wanted to experiment with different genres and different kinds of characters. So, it's not that I will avoid playing similar characters in different films. They may sound similar in some ways or share certain mannerisms, but the entire psyche of the character can be different. I would like to experiment with those finer nuances of characters.

On top of that, I have never felt that I need to take a break from working with Hansal. In fact, actors dream to work with a director like him. He lets you do whatever you feel like, depending on your confidence in the script and each and every line. He also lets you explore things in detail. He never tells you to do only this or that, unless something isn't flowing. As an star, you enjoy the whole process because he puts so much trust in you. His process is extremely organic. I love his storytelling, which has interesting and subtle layers in every movie he makes and everything of his that I have seen.

I get this question a lot, but I don't feel nervous or pressurised. I certainly feel that a lot of responsibility comes with playing these characters. My job is not to judge them. I have to create these characters for the audience to judge and explore.

title: Ramayana box office collection day 20: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film bounces back with 28% jump on third Tuesday, inches closer to ₹1,000 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ranbir Kapoor, Yash movie Ramayana records 28% jump, ₹1,000 crore rupees milestone beckons. more Ramayana ticket-window earnings The movie has collected an estimated ₹ 971.56 crore rupees in India net so far, putting it within touching distance of the milestone. Its third Tuesday brought in ₹ 16.11 crore rupees. The Hindi version accounted for the biggest share, earning ₹ 14.34 crore rupees from 13,544 shows. The Kannada version collected ₹ 83 lakh from 445 shows, while Tamil and Telugu brought in ₹ 58 lakh and ₹ 36 lakh from 571 and 425 shows, respectively.

Adding to this, The Tuesday figures are higher than Monday's collection of ₹ 12.70 crore rupees, showing a rise of around 26.85% from the previous day. The movie's net collection stands at ₹ 971.56 crore rupees. The movie is inching towards ₹ 1,000 crore rupees club in India.

Meanwhile, Titled Ramayana: Rise of a Legend in international markets, the movie is the first part of a two-movie adaptation of the Hindu epic. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi is seen as Goddess Sita and Yash portrays Ravana. The cast also includes Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, Rakul Preet Singh as Surpanakha, Lara Dutta as Queen Kaikeyi, Arun Govil as King Dashrath and Kajal Aggarwal as Mandodari.

Notably, The movie is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash under the banners of Prime Focus Studios and Monster Mind Creations. DNEG and ReDefine have handled the visual effects, while the music has been composed by Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman.

As per the latest buzz, The second installment is scheduled to rollout during Diwali 2028. In an interview with E! News, producer Namit Malhotra explained why the team decided to give the sequel an extra year. He shared, "So the idea was now that we've got so much excitement that the world has had, we want to take a little bit more time to make sure that when we present the grand finale, we have a little bit more time to do what we did on part one. That extra year is what I genuinely believe we need to do justice for a movie of this size. When you see part 2 coming in, that will be a whole other story. We didn't want to do a rush job or get ahead of ourselves. We want to deliver the finale in the most grand way that it deserves."

title: AICWA writes to PM Narendra Modi seeking ban on Fawad Khan and Mahira Khan starrer Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo on Netflix India
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:
The body has urged the government to enforce the May 2025 advisory on Pakistani-origin content and introduce a permanent law restricting its rollout across Indian platforms.

Adding to this, Dated November 24, 2026, the two-page letter is signed by AICWA President Suresh Shyamlal Gupta and has also been marked to Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Netflix India. The association shared copies of the letter through its official X account on Tuesday, reiterating its opposition to the streaming of Pakistani shows, films, music and podcasts in the country.

Meanwhile, In its accompanying post, AICWA shared, “Terror Gets No Applause. Nation Comes First. The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) has written to Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji, demanding that the Pakistani series "Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo" is not rolled out on Netflix in India on 4 December 2026. Pakistan was, is and will remain a terrorist country. Its series, films, songs, podcasts and all other content have no place on Indian screens. We have also demanded a strong, permanent law with the severest penalties, and we appeal to Netflix India and all OTT platforms never to show any Pakistani content in India. Nation Comes First. Always.”

Notably, In its letter, the association referred to the 2019 Pulwama attack and the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam terror attack while explaining its objection to the series’ proposed Indian rollout. It also cited the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting’s advisory dated May 8, 2025, which directed OTT platforms, streaming services and intermediaries operating in India to discontinue Pakistani-origin content. AICWA argued that making the series available to Indian audiences would go against the spirit of the advisory and national sentiment.
As per the latest buzz, 🇮🇳 Terror Gets No Applause. Nation Comes First. 🇮🇳

In further updates, The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) has written to Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji, demanding that the Pakistani series "Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo" is not rolled out on Netflix in India on 4 December 2026.
On top of that, Pakistan was, is and will remain a terrorist country. Its series, films, songs, podcasts and all other content have no place on Indian screens.
We have also demanded a strong, permanent law with the severest penalties, and we appeal to Netflix India and all OTT platforms never to show any Pakistani content in India.

title: Hindu outfits protest, BJP slams Vijay govt after Karthigai Deepam not lit at SC-approved spot
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The lamp was lit at the Uchipillayar Temple instead of the Deepathoon stone pillar. (HT) more The top court had designated ‘Deepathoon’, the disputed stone pillar on the Thiruparankundram hill, for the lighting of the lamp as part of a one-time arrangement this year.

Adding to this, District authorities lit the ceremonial lamp at the Deepa Mandapam at the Uchipillayar Kovil, a hilltop shrine on the Thiruparankundram Hill at 6pm. This has been the usual spot for the lamp lighting every year, but the top court had granted an exception this time.
Meanwhile, Devotees and members of Hindu organisations who were gathered in large numbers, staged a protest demanding that ceremonial lamp be lit at the Deepathoon.

Notably, However, police personnel detained them and forced them to enter into the police vehicle. The agitating protesters raised slogans against the TVK government as they were being taken away by the police personnel.
As per the latest buzz, The BJP and the AIADMK also hit out at the TVK-led state government over it.

In further updates, The BJP alleged that the failure to light the Karthigai Deepam at the stone pillar was a defiance of the Supreme Court and sought accountability from CM Vijay-led government. BJP's national general secretary BL Santhosh also targeted the Madurai DM.
On top of that, "The TVK government will face both civilisational and legal challenge. They have bit more than they can chew," Santhosh shared in a tweet in Tamil.

As Tamil Nadu minister CTR Nirmal Kumar verified the lighting of the lamp at the usual spot, BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan shared: “It is highly condemnable for a person holding the office of Law Minister to openly oppose an interim order of the Supreme Court. The Tamil Nadu Law Minister has forfeited the moral right to continue in that office.”

title: Ramayana earns two spots on Critics Choice Awards shortlists alongside The Odyssey and Dune Part Three
body: Here's the latest update from the Hollywood/Marvel world:

The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer Ramayana has made it to two technical shortlists for the 32nd Annual Critics Choice Awards, competing in the Best Visual Effects and Best Stunt Design categories. more Ramayana shares the shortlist with The Odyssey and Dune: Part Three The movie, known as Ramayana: Rise of a Legend in international markets, has been recognised for its technical work, with Dan Glass credited for the visual effects. The selection is an important moment for the movie, particularly as it finds a place in craft categories that often see competition from big-budget Hollywood productions.

Adding to this, Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey has made the strongest showing among the shortlisted films, earning mentions in 11 of the 12 categories. Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part Three and the Spanish-language movie La Bola Negra have secured eight mentions each. Meanwhile, Godzilla Minus Zero and Laika's animated feature Wildwood have found a place in seven categories apiece.

Meanwhile, In the Best Visual Effects category, Ramayana will compete with films including Dune: Part Three, The Odyssey, Godzilla Minus Zero, Project Hail Mary, Spider-Man: Brand New Day and Wildwood. The movie has also been shortlisted for Best Stunt Design, alongside titles such as Dune: Part Three, The Odyssey, Godzilla Minus Zero and Jackass: Best and Last. Its presence in both categories brings attention to the scale of the technical work involved in making the mythological epic.

Notably, The shortlists are not the final nominations. They are part of the first round of selection, with a special nominating committee picking 59 films for 144 places across 12 categories. These include cinematography, editing, production design, costume design, hair and makeup, visual effects, sound, original score, original song, casting, ensemble and stunt design.

As per the latest buzz, The final nominations will be revealed on December 4, with six films competing in each technical category. The 32nd Annual Critics Choice Awards will take place on January 3, 2027, at the Barker Hangar in Santa Monica. Comedian Janelle James will host the ceremony, which will be broadcast live.

In further updates, Ramayana: Part 1 is the first of Nitesh Tiwari's two-movie adaptation of the Hindu epic. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi stars as Goddess Sita and Yash portrays Ravana. The movie also features Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, Rakul Preet Singh as Surpanakha, Lara Dutta as Queen Kaikeyi, Arun Govil as King Dashrath and Kajal Aggarwal as Mandodari.

On top of that, Namit Malhotra and Yash have produced the movie under Prime Focus Studios and Monster Mind Creations. DNEG and ReDefine have worked on the visual effects, while the music features compositions by Oscar-winning musicians Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman. The story will continue with Ramayana: Part 2, which is slated to arrive in theatres during Diwali 2028.

title: Karan Johar defends Deepika Padukone's 8-hour shift demand, says female stars deserve equal rights
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Karan Johar backs Deepika Padukone's 8-hour shift demand. more Karan Johar praises Akshay Kumar Karan Johar dismissed the rumours surrounding Akshay Kumar’s famous early-morning routine, instead praising the star’s discipline and dedication to his work. Recalling his experience of working with Akshay, Karan shared, “When I did my first movie with Akshay, there was always talks making the rounds that Akshay Kumar does this, Akshay Kumar does that. Firstly, I've never seen a man work this hard. He has meetings at 5:00 a.m. He knows his script by heart, and he's always supportive of the director and very cognizant of the producer. And he's the only superstar that gives a chance to a debut director, and that's one thing that he doesn't get enough credit for.”

Adding to this, Drawing a parallel between Akshay Kumar’s disciplined work schedule and the debate around working hours in the movie industry, Karan shared female actors should be given the same respect and flexibility as their male counterparts. According to a report in Screen, he backed Deepika Padukone’s stance on working hours, saying, “That's why I also respect someone like Deepika Padukone's decision. When she says something like this, I don't know why it's made into such a big deal. It's her right. She's collected that right. She's a hardworking woman. She's a mother, she's a wife, she's a professional, and she has a personal life. Why can't she ask for it when you ask for it? There is sometimes this gender disparity that happens, and it's not fair.”

Meanwhile, Karan added that female superstars should have the same freedom to set work-related boundaries as their male counterparts. He pointed out that producers choose to work with actors such as Deepika Padukone and Akshay Kumar because they admire their work and respect their achievements.

Notably, Akshay agreed with Karan’s perspective, backing the eight-hour shift model for actors. He shared disciplined, time-bound shoots benefit everyone on set without compromising the creative output.

As per the latest buzz, The duo also drew parallels with international filmmaking standards, noting how major Hollywood productions, from Tom Cruise’s action films to Christopher Nolan’s large-scale projects, operate on tightly planned shooting schedules. The full episode of Koffee With Karan Season 9 will stream this Wednesday at 7 pm on JioHotstar.

In further updates, In 2025, reports suggested that Deepika exited Sandeep Reddy Vanga’s Spirit after a dispute with the makers over working hours. She as per reports sought an eight-hour work shift, but the makers were unable to accommodate her request. She was subsequently verified to be out of the sequel to Kalki 2898 AD as well.

On top of that, Deepika later broke her silence on the eight-hour work shift debate in an interview with CNBC-TV18 in October 2025. Defending her demand, she pointed out that several male superstars in the industry had followed eight-hour shifts for years without facing similar scrutiny. She shared that being a woman should not make her request seem pushy. Deepika received support from several Bollywood actors, including Kareena Kapoor, Ananya Panday, Neha Dhupia and Alia Bhatt.

title: Imtiaz Ali says younger actors in Bollywood are more 'undistracted'; it is easier to coach them for a long-term job than senior stars
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Imtiaz Ali at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit, in conversation about his films and more. (HT Photo) more Imtiaz Ali defends younger actors At HTLS 2026, Imtiaz was asked if there is any difference in the focus and attention spans of younger actors as compared to older stars. “I feel that if attention spans are declining, they are declining for everyone alive, not just the younger generation. All of us are experiencing a shorter attention span. On the other hand, I feel younger people are more used to this because this generation was born post-internet and with all the devices we have on our bodies right now. So, they are used to it. We stumbled upon it. We became distracted, and some of us became loony,” the star shared.

Adding to this, Imtiaz appeared at the summit with star Ananya Panday . Talking about the actors of her generation, the filmmaker added, “They can adapt to this world much better. We keep talking about the younger generation being distracted or not wanting a long-term situation in their lives. On the other hand, I found that younger actors are the most undisturbed while working. When they dedicate themselves to work, I don't see them being distracted by anything. Telling them to do a long-term job is not more difficult. It's actually easier than with the older actors.”

Meanwhile, Imtiaz of late worked with two young actors - Vedang Raina and Sharvari - in Main Vaapas Aaunga. The movie also starred veteran Naseeruddin Shah and Diljit Dosanjh. In the past, Imtiaz has directed several older stars, including Ranbir Kapoor, Shah Rukh Khan, Deepika Padukone, Anushka Sharma, Shahid Kapoor, and Kareena Kapoor.

Notably, Ananya also echoed what Imtiaz shared on stage. “I think Gen-Z is badnaam (infamous) for no reason,” she shared, smiling. There is a sense that young people do not want to fight hard for success, she added, but “it’s just our definition of success that’s different. Earlier, the sentiment was that if you hadn’t slogged mentally and physically, you hadn’t worked hard enough.”

As per the latest buzz, Imtiaz is currently awaiting the rollout of his web series, O Saathi Re. Written and created by Imtiaz and directed by Arif Ali, O Saathi Re is a Window Seat Films production featuring Aditi Rao Hydari, Avinash Tiwary, and Arjun Rampal. The series explores the complexities of love, personal desires, power dynamics and the imbalance that can exist within relationships. It premieres on Netflix on December 4.

In further updates, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). With a good understanding of cinema and its trends, and a keen eye for detail, he continues to spark conversations around showbiz for readers around the world.

title: Hrithik Roshan’s father Rakesh Roshan’s firm leases Mumbai office space at ₹7 lakh monthly rent to Fuji Silvertech Concrete Private Limited
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Rakesh Roshan-led Filmkraft Productions has leased a 2,727 sq ft commercial office space at Lotus Corporate Park in Mumbai's Goregaon East to Fuji Silvertech Concrete for a five-year term. (PTI Photo)(PTI10_31_2026_000211A) (Representative photo) (PTI) more The bare-shell office premises, located on a higher floor of the commercial complex, have a carpet area of 2,727 sq ft and come with three basement parking spaces. The leave and licence agreement was registered on November 13, 2026, with Filmkraft Productions represented by director Rakesh Roshan Nagrath and Fuji Silvertech Concrete represented by its chief strategy officer, Brijmohan Gopaldas Soni.

Adding to this, The agreement includes an interest-free, refundable security deposit of ₹ 42 lakh, equivalent to six months' initial rent. The licence commenced on November 16, 2026, while the rent commencement date is January 16, 2027. The tenant has been granted a two-month rent-free period for interior and fit-out work. The agreement also provides for an annual rent escalation of 5%, the documents showed.
Meanwhile, Rakesh Roshan and Fuji Silvertech Concrete Private Limited could not be reached for comment.

Notably, Earlier, Rakesh Roshan had leased two commercial units in Andheri West, Mumbai, to Beingu Studios Private Limited for 36 months at a combined monthly licence fee of ₹ 7.30 lakh, according to registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix.

As per the latest buzz, The two units are located at Commerce Centre, off New Link Road in Oshiwara, Andheri West, and have a combined area of 5,574 sq ft. The agreement includes two car parking spaces and an interest-free security deposit of ₹ 10.95 lakh.

In further updates, Registered on September 9, 2026, the leave and licence agreement provides for a 5% annual escalation. The monthly licence fee will increase to ₹ 7.66 lakh in the second year and ₹ 8.04 lakh in the third year, the documents showed.

On top of that, A few months earlier, Rakesh Roshan and his wife, Pramila Roshan, had leased their apartment in Mumbai's Juhu-Vile Parle Development (JVPD) Scheme for three years. The lease is expected to generate rental income of approximately ₹ 1.89 crore rupees over the tenure, according to property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix.

The Roshan family, including Rakesh Roshan and star Hrithik Roshan, has been active in Mumbai's real estate market, particularly in commercial property transactions. In January 2026, Rakesh Roshan sold a 1.09-hectare land parcel in Pune district for ₹ 15 crore rupees, according to registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix.

Sooraj Barjatya and Salman Khan to reunite for Prem Ki Shaadi. more Sooraj Barjatya talks about Prem Ki Shaadi In a recent interview with the Free Press Journal, Sooraj shared an update on the movie with Salman and shared, “Abhi thoda sa wakht aur hai, kyunki thoda aur mujhe kuch cheezein polish karni hai (There’s still a little time left because I need to polish a few more things)."

Adding to this, In 2022, when Salman attended the screening of Sooraj Barjatya’s Uunchai, he opened up that the two would soon collaborate on a movie. When the filmmaker shared, “Prem will return”, he opened up that he had also registered the title. Salman then added that Prem would return and Sooraj would make sure he got married, too. Meanwhile, Before this, Sooraj had directed Salman in several blockbusters, including Maine Pyar Kiya, Hum Aapke Hain Koun..!, Hum Saath-Saath Hain and Prem Ratan Dhan Payo. In all these films, Salman played the iconic character of Prem.

Notably, Produced by Rajshri Productions in association with Mahaveer Jain Films, the movie marks Sooraj Barjatya’s return to direction after Uunchai, which won a National Award. The movie stars Ayushmann as Prem, a man who stands up for his new bride after she refuses to move in with her in-laws because she wants to take care of her own family. Sharvari plays the female lead. The movie also features Anupam Kher, Supriya Pathak Kapur, Seema Pahwa, Swanand Kirkire, Saumya Tandon, Shruti Seth, Shaad Randhawa, Girish Kulkarni and Rajesh Kumar in key roles.

As per the latest buzz, Ever since the movie’s trailer was rolled out, it has been compared to Karan Johar’s Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani. Addressing the comparisons at the trailer launch event, Ayushmann shared, “This is a Sooraj Barjatya movie, and Prem is a green flag. In this movie (Yeh Prem Mol Liya), he is someone who takes a stand for his wife's family. Rocky's character arc in Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani is different. Prem is very different from him. You cannot even compare the two.”

In further updates, Ayushmann is the sixth star to play Prem in a Sooraj Barjatya movie. Before him, Salman, Abhishek Bachchan, Hrithik Roshan, Sonu Sood and Shahid Kapoor won audiences over with their performances as Prem. title: IFFI 2026: Ayan Mukerji BREAKS silence on Brahmastra’s mixed reception: “If there were things audiences didn’t like, probably they were things we needed to improve in the storytelling”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ayan Mukerji shared, "If I had to be completely honest, yeah, I had a mixed feeling when the movie came out. I had experienced with a movie like say Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani (2013). I know what a gold medal is when you get it from the audience. But with Brahmastra , it was a slightly rockier landing. There were things which people liked about the movie a lot and there were certain things that they did not like as much. Some people liked it more. Some people liked it less."

Adding to this, He added, "However, I never think that the audience fails the movie. I truly believe that the audience is always king. You have to always respect what the audience senses in a movie, even if it doesn't go in your favour."

Meanwhile, Ayan Mukerji further shared, "And I feel in India, even if you don't agree with them, we need to understand that our audiences are very smart. So if there were things they didn't like, probably they were things we needed to improve in the storytelling."

(PTI) more Shabana Azmi’s stance on burqa On the Known Unknown podcast by Usha Kadake, Shabana was asked about receiving flak in the past for talking about Muslim women and burqa. The star replied, “It’s nowhere written in the Quran that burqas should be worn a certain way. It’s written in the Quran that there should be modesty in your gaze, for both men and women. It’s the middlemen who present it as something else and cause confusion about the religion.”

Adding to this, She then shared, however, that women should have the right to choose how they dress without being mandated to dress a certain way. “But I also believe that…now, I don’t wear a burqa. But if you tell me that I don't have the right to wear one, then I'll wear three burqas. Who are you? Who are you to tell me? It cannot happen that you promote fundamentalism under the guise of secularism. That cannot happen,” shared Shabana.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shabana Azmi (@azmishabana18)

Notably, In 2022, six Muslim students at a government pre-university college in Udipi, Karnataka, were barred from attending classes in hijab. The government also issued an order mandating strict adherence to school uniforms, leading to protests and court cases. Kangana Ranaut and Shabana even exchanged views on it on social media. Shabana was criticised for defending it while she herself does not wear a hijab.

As per the latest buzz, Her husband, Javed Akhtar , had also chimed in on the discourse back then, writing on X (formerly Twitter), “I have never been in favour of Hijab or Burqa. I still stand by that but at the same time I have nothing but deep contempt for these mobs of hooligans who are trying to intimidate a small group of girls and that too unsuccessfully. Is this their idea of “MANLINESS” . What a pity.”

In further updates, Shabana starred in Rajkumar Santoshi’s Batwara 1947 and Nitin Kakkar’s Awarapan 2 this year. The former also stars Sunny Deol and Preity Zinta in lead roles. It opened to lukewarm reviews and grossed ₹ 54.20 crore rupees worldwide. Awarapan 2 starred Emraan Hashmi and Disha Patani in lead roles. Receiving mixed reviews, it grossed ₹ 213 crore rupees worldwide.

On top of that, Despite having a Master's degree in Journalism and over a decade of experience in print and digital media as a field reporter and sub-editor at organisations such as The Times of India and Reader's Digest, Neeshita Nyayapati remains a movie buff first and a Chief Content Producer second. She fell in love with movies in childhood and believes nothing matches the magic of watching a good movie that moves you with a warm tub of popcorn in hand. Her love for writing about cinema follows that. Come Friday, you'll find her at her happy place, the movies, catching the latest rom-com or masala offering, for reviews or otherwise. While her niche is Telugu cinema, Neeshita likes to dabble in a little bit of everything to stay up to date. From movie announcements to scandals and hard news angles, she has explored it all. title: Shruti Haasan addresses Peddi controversy as she insists she refuses costumes and choreography she is uncomfortable with: “I am okay with being called difficult”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Speaking about her appearance in the song ‘Hellallallo’, the star discusses conversation around dance numbers in mainstream cinema.

Adding to this, In an interview with Galatta Plus, Haasan was asked whether she questions the need for special dance tracks in films, particularly in the context of the discussion sparked by Peddi . She clarified that while she does question the convention, her participation in such sequences comes from her own enjoyment of dancing and dressing up, rather than a desire to meet external expectations.

Meanwhile, Explaining her approach to visual presentation and personal boundaries, Shruti shared, “I have always asked that question. I enjoy dancing; let me be very, very clear. I enjoy dressing up. And that’s the approach that I have to it. My approach to visual sexuality has been very liberating for myself. I have never been a panderer in any capacity. So, when I’m not comfortable with something, I’m gonna say I’m not gonna wear this. Rest assured, I am doing it; I am comfortable with it. If I’m uncomfortable, I am not gonna do it. I’ve had arguments about it; I’ve been called difficult for it. And I am okay with it."

Notably, The star also acknowledged the larger conversation around item songs, the male gaze and the expectations placed on performers. However, she pointed out that the tendency to cater to external expectations is not limited to dance sequences or revealing costumes. Elaborating on her views, she added, “I understand the discourse around it. But genuinely, my approach to it is: I have fun dancing, I have fun doing choreography, I have fun being sexy. It’s not with a pandering gaze. Is it just in item songs? I mean, we are pandering in many, many capacities. Not just the tiny clothes in an item song. We live in a pandering world currently. So you choose your pander or don’t choose your pander."

As per the latest buzz, The discussion comes amid the response to Peddi , which drew criticism on social media over the presentation of Janhvi Kapoor’s character, Achiyamma. During an appearance on Koffee With Karan Season 9, Kapoor also reflected on the row, saying she wished she had been more vocal about refusing sequences that made her uncomfortable. She acknowledged that she could have pushed back more firmly at the time.

In further updates, Haasan’s comments add another perspective to the ongoing conversation, highlighting the distinction between an star’s personal comfort with a performance and the broader questions audiences raise about how women are presented in commercial cinema.

title: Hema Malini on Dharmendra's first death anniversary: ‘my grief has not lost its intensity, life feels empty’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Hema Malini with late Dharmendra Check out the post:

Adding to this, View this post on Instagram Remembering Dharmendra, she wrote, “A whole year has sped by but my grief has not lost its intensity I grieve over the tremendous and irreparable loss of a man who was not just my husband - he was my everything -my friend, philosopher and guide who was my backbone and in short, was my very existence. Life seems so empty without him. His towering personality, his innate goodness that pervaded his whole being and spread his love towards all who knew him - such a unique human being who, though he reached the pinnacle of success, remained grounded and attached to his roots.”

I am aware of this, but I am still here in this life, and I cannot but miss his loving presence. I thank all the millions of followers who have recalled this generous, lovely human being and sent such warm notes about Dharam ji and what he meant to them.”

Notably, Dharmendra passed away on November 24, 2025, at the age of 89, leaving behind a legacy spanning more than six decades in Indian cinema. One of Hindi cinema's most loved stars, the star was celebrated for his versatility and screen presence.

title: Ramayana makers slash ticket prices by up to 80% as Ranbir Kapoor, Yash-starrer finally loses steam at the box office
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Ravie Dubey. more Ramayana ticket prices slashed to ₹ 99 On Monday, the movie's official Instagram account shared a poster announcing a reduction in ticket prices. “Experience Ramayana on the big screen this Tuesday, with tickets starting at just ₹ 99*. Wishing everyone a blessed Gurpurab ,” read the caption. Gurpurab, a Sikh festival, falls on Tuesday. The creative alongside featured the movie’s poster with the text: “This Tuesday just got epic. Tickets starting at just ₹ 99.”

Adding to this, Following the announcement, most halls across India reduced the ticket prices for their Ramayana shows to as low as ₹ 99. Theatres in metros like Mumbai and Delhi, which had been selling 2D show tickets for as high as ₹ 300-400, now have tickets flat at ₹ 99. In most places, the price reduction is over 50-60%, while in some halls, it is as high as 80%.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by The World Of Ramayana (@worldoframayana)

Notably, Premium tickets like recliner seats are still priced higher, up to about ₹ 199-249. Similarly, 3D and IMAX shows also continue to have higher ticket prices. Prices for 3D shows in Mumbai and Delhi range from ₹ 119 to ₹ 249, much lower than the original ₹ 500+ rate. IMAX 3D rates have also come down to as low as ₹ 250 in some screens. Others, however, retain premium ticket rates of ₹ 700-800.

As per the latest buzz, BookMyShow shows that the reduced ticket prices are in effect for the remainder of the week, not just Tuesday. It remains unclear as to whether and when the ticket rates will be hiked again. Ramayana is running in around 4000 screens across India, and is in its third week in theatres.

In further updates, Ramayana took a roaring start at the domestic ticket-window, minting ₹ 238 crore rupees in its four-day extended opening weekend. It then saw a huge jump during the post-Diwali break, adding ₹ 325 crore rupees over the next four days. The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer had a strong second weekend as well, but lost momentum over the weekdays. On November 23, its third Monday, Ramayana dropped by 64% to earn just ₹ 12.70 crore rupees on the day. This is an 89% drop from its peak performance of ₹ 107.50 crore rupees on its first Monday.
On top of that, Despite the slowdown, Ramayana has still managed to earn ₹ 955 crore rupees net in India and over ₹ 1700 crore rupees gross worldwide.

Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is the first of a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. Part 2 is scheduled to rollout in 2028.

title: Jeetendra says son Tusshar Kapoor is a better and more dedicated actor than him, credits his own success to luck
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Jeetendra says Tusshar Kapoor is a better star than him. more Jeetendra praises son Tusshar Kapoor When asked about Tusshar's relatively limited success compared to his own, Jeetendra shared, “It is all destiny. Tusshar is a far better and far more dedicated star than I ever was, and I am not saying this just because he is my son. I was simply lucky to be in the right place at the right time. Think of what would have happened to me if the great V. Shantaramji had not spotted me and made me a hero. I had no experience, no talent, nothing—only luck on my side.”

Adding to this, Jeetendra began his acting journey with V. Shantaram's Geet Gaya Patharon Ne (1964), before achieving stardom with Farz (1967). His energetic dance moves in the 70s collected him the nickname 'Jumping Jack of Bollywood'.

Meanwhile, Jeetendra further revealed whether he had ever guided Tusshar in his career, saying, "Tusshar is a very sensible and very focused boy. He never needed my advice. It was Ektaa I used to worry about! When she was younger, she did only three things: eat, eat and eat. She would even polish off her brother’s tiffin. I never thought she would be where she is today. Do you know she does charitable work and runs an old-age home without ever talking about it? I am very proud of both my children. I have now involved Tusshar in the construction business that I am running."

Notably, Jeetendra remains one of the most popular stars of Hindi cinema, particularly remembered for his remarkable run during the 1970s and 1980s. He established himself as a bankable commercial star with films such as Caravan, Humjoli, Jeene Ki Raah, Bidaai, Dharam Veer, Himmatwala, Tohfa, Maqsad, Meri Aawaz Suno and Swarg Narak.

As per the latest buzz, Tusshar Kapoor followed in his father's footsteps into Bollywood but carved out a very different career. Unlike Jeetendra, who became a leading man and a major commercial star during his time, Tusshar's journey has largely been defined by supporting roles, ensemble films and comedy. He made his acting debut with Mujhe Kucch Kehna Hai (2001). While he went on to feature in films such as Khakee, Shootout at Lokhandwala, The Dirty Picture and Shor in the City, his most popular screen persona emerged through the Golmaal franchise, in which he plays the mute character Lucky.

Ravie Dubey essays the role of Lakshman in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. more Mukesh Chhabra praises Ravie Dubey Mukesh is in Goa for the ongoing International Movie Festival of India (IFFI), where he spoke to news agency ANI about his approach to casting and some choice that he was proud of. Mukesh was the casting director for that movie as well. “He (Ravie) reminded me of what I did with Sushant in Kai Po Che!, what I did with Rajkummar, what I did with many other actors. title: Sonu Nigam buys commercial property in Mumbai for Rs. 31.47 crores: Report

Its strategic location near prominent neighbourhoods and business hubs such as Bandra, Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC), Juhu, Vile Parle, and Andheri further enhances its appeal. title: IFFI 2026: Ayan Mukerji CONFIRMS Brahmastra 2; hopes it will be "more Indian"; reveals Brahmastra's OTT version has longer scenes than theatrical cut; admits, "Overthinking is not always improving"
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

He shared, "As we step into Brahmastra 2 , I hope we can make it even more Indian. What happened with me when I began Brahmastra was that there were certain Western influences in mind. There were stories from the West which I enjoyed like Harry Potter , to give you an example. Also, they (Hollywood) dabbled more in this genre in these last 10-15 years. They were doing more superhero and fantasy films. In Brahmastra , there was a touch of Hinduism and Indian spirituality which was a part of the writing. As I started writing, I realized that it's an interesting original stuff that started to call me more and more. That's why, the movie was originally called Dragon and it got rechristened to Brahmastra ."

Adding to this, He also opened up that one can enjoy a longer version of Brahmastra on digital. He shared, "The movie I put out on streaming is a slightly different edit than the one we rolled out in cinema. Because I was watching the movie again and again and again, we edited certain scenes in a very sharp way when we put it out in cinemas. Honestly, I had seen those scenes so many times myself that by the time I was watching it for the 500th time, I knew every beat of the scene. So, I was finding the scenes a little bit slow. I thought, 'Let me cut the pauses of the actors. Let me make it go faster and faster'."

Meanwhile, He revealed, "To those scenes, I got a very different reaction from the audience when they saw the movie as compared to when I had shown the movie to a lot of people in the office. That's because the movie that they were seeing was a different movie than the final version that I had put out. So, that was a note to myself that sometimes, you feel that you are improving something. But overthinking is not always improving."

title: Ramayana box office collection day 19: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash film sees 64% dip on 3rd Monday, inches closer to ₹1,000 crore mark
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ranbir Kapoor wearing Assam's handmade cane-rubber armour in Ramayana. more Ramayana ticket-window earnings According to trade estimates, the movie has collected nearly ₹ 955 crore rupees net in India. Rolled out on November 5, 2026, the movie had a massive opening during the Diwali festive period. Although collections slowed down during the weekdays in its third week, the movie witnessed a jump over the weekend, bringing it closer to the ₹ 1,000 crore rupees milestone. The Hindi version continues to contribute the most to its overall earnings, followed by its dubbed releases in other languages.

Adding to this, On Day 19, Ramayana collected an estimated ₹ 12.70 crore rupees net in India across approximately 15,690 shows, facing 64% dip from day 18. The Hindi version brought in ₹ 9.25 crore rupees from 13,439 shows, making it the biggest contributor for the day. The Malayalam version collected ₹ 1.50 crore rupees from 824 shows, while Kannada collected ₹ 85 lakh across 438 shows. Tamil added ₹ 80 lakh from 565 shows, and Telugu contributed another ₹ 30 lakh from 424 shows. With these collections, the movie's total India net collection reached ₹ 955.45 crore rupees.

Meanwhile, Ramayana: Part 1, also titled Ramayana: Rise of a Legend in international markets, is the first instalment of Nitesh Tiwari's two-part adaptation of the Hindu epic. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi portrays Goddess Sita and Yash appears as Ravana. The movie also features Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, Rakul Preet Singh as Surpanakha, Lara Dutta as Queen Kaikeyi, Arun Govil as King Dashrath and Kajal Aggarwal as Mandodari.

Notably, Produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash under Prime Focus Studios and Monster Mind Creations, the movie's visual effects have been created by DNEG and ReDefine. The music brings together Oscar-winning composers Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman. The makers have verified that the second installment, Ramayana: Part 2, will rollout during Diwali 2028.

As per the latest buzz, In an interview with E! News, producer Namit Malhotra explained why the team has decided to take an additional year to complete the sequel. He shared, “So the idea was now that we've got so much excitement that the world has had, we want to take a little bit more time to make sure that when we present the grand finale, we have a little bit more time to do what we did on part one. We didn't want to do a rush job or get ahead of ourselves. We want to deliver the finale in the most grand way that it deserves.”

title: Often praised for her looks, Tamannaah Bhatia questions what beauty truly means
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Tamannaah Bhatia has received praise for her beauty and colour, sometimes in a misogynistic manner. more Tamannaah Bhatia questions the meaning of beauty Tamannaah asked Sadhguru whether beauty is inherited or created. She asked, “I bump into people, and they look at me, and they think I am beautiful. How we end up looking by the end of our lives, is that something that has been given to us or something that we are creating?”

Adding to this, “About the genetic advantage that somebody may have of whatever kind of nose or chin or whatever you have, that does not entirely decide,” answered Sadhguru, adding, “It decides some aspects of it, but the rest of it is how an individual makes them, himself or herself. Because you may have whatever kind of nose or chin, but if you look at this, a joyful face is always a beautiful face. Isn’t it? That all of us can do. See, even I managed with all this (points to his long beard).”
Meanwhile, Tamannaah insisted that Sadhguru was beautiful, making him laugh.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sadhguru (@sadhguru)

As per the latest buzz, While promoting her movie 2025 movie Odela 2 in which she played a sadhvi, Tamannaah responded to a reporter’s question about being a ‘milky beauty’. “You are saying milky beauty, but why did you look at a milky beauty and think that she can't be a Shiva Shakti? Your question contains the answer. He [director Ashok Teja] does not look at milky beauty as something to be ashamed of or feel bad about” She also shared that glamour in women must be celebrated, adding, “If we look at ourselves in a certain way, then nobody can respect us.”

In further updates, In April, she addressed a question of whether being known for her looks has been limiting as an star. She shared, “I just do not like being in victim mode and saying I am not getting opportunities because I am so beautiful and all that. That just sounds very strange to me.” In October last year, Annu Kapoor referred to her ‘dudhiya badan’ (fair and beautiful body) while talking about her song Aaj Ki Raat on Shubhankar Mishra's YouTube channel. He received massive backlash for his comment.

On top of that, Speaking at NDTV Profit Ignite later that month, Tamannaah addressed sexist remarks about her looks and shared, “I think that as a creative person, our most important task is to listen. And when we listen, what we keep and what we filter is very important to understand. And because you are also a woman, you can understand that if we start giving importance to such things, then perhaps we will not be able to move forward in life.”
Tamannaah last starred in The Vvaan : Force of the Forrest. She has Ragini 3, Rangers, Purushan, IPS Maria and V Shantaram lined up.

title: Kaali Kheti review: Jackie Shroff, Sharad Kelkar's horror drama delivers unconventional scares, albeit in bits
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Jackie Shroff and Sharad Kelkar in a still from Kaali Kheti. more Kaali Kheti story Directed by Haris Imtiyaz Khan, the story revolves around Babuji ( Jackie Shroff ), who returns to his village after a decade. His son ( Sharad Kelkar ), a farmer like his father, is struggling to get a decent yield from his land. Babuji promises to help him turn things around. Meanwhile, he encounters an old friend who has lost his mental balance, with his body gradually turning black. The man soon dies, and Babuji begins experiencing similar symptoms. His quest to uncover the mystery behind the bizarre phenomenon forms the rest of the story.

Adding to this, The subject is unique, and the movie attempts to weave horror with a commentary on the plight of farmers, who continue to struggle to make ends meet. The rural setting lends the narrative an unsettling quality, while the idea of something sinister lurking beneath the very land that sustains these families makes for an interesting premise.

Meanwhile, The pacing is largely on point, and the movie deserves credit for not resorting to the usual horror movie tropes. It attempts to build an atmosphere of dread rather than solely relying on jump scares.

Notably, However, the writing, especially in the climax, doesn't do justice to the premise. The movie gets caught up in its central idea and leaves the viewer underwhelmed when it should ideally have been exhilarating.

As per the latest buzz, Among the performances, Jackie Shroff nails the part as the man connected to his roots. His real-life persona, as a nature lover, helps the story immensely. Sharad Kelkar as his son, who is hiding a dark secret, does justice. Neha Sargam as Radha is also effective.
In further updates, The special effects are also okay and serviceable.

On top of that, Overall, Kaali Kheti has an intriguing idea at its core. The rural setting and the connection between the land and the people who depend on it give the movie a distinct identity. The performances, particularly Shroff's, lend the story emotional weight. However, a promising premise can only take a movie so far, and the writing ultimately struggles to deliver a payoff that matches the mystery it builds. The result is moments of unease, but never quite as haunting as it could have been.
